questions.q:
Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.

(SSC MTS 2024 S.37_23-Oct_Shift-2)
o: The Nile is the long river in the world with a length about approximately 6650 km.
The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length of approximately 6650 km.
The Nile is the most long river in the world of a length of approximately 6650 km.
The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length about approximately 6650 km.
questions.s:
Answer:The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length of approximately 6650 km.

Explanation:
This sentence is grammatically correct and clear in meaning. Let’s break it down:

  • "The longest river" is the correct superlative form of "long" (not "long" or "most long").

  • "with a length of approximately" is the correct phrase. We use "of" after "length", not "about".

  • "approximately" already means "about", so using both is redundant.

Now, why the others are incorrect:

  • "The Nile is the long river..." – ❌ incorrect; should be "longest" for superlative.

  • "most long" – ❌ not used; use "longest" instead.

  • "about approximately" – ❌ redundant; use only one.

Correct sentence:
The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length of approximately 6650 km.

questions.q: The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.
o: are most bitterer
questions.s:
Answer: are most bitterer

Explanation:
The phrase "most bitterer" is incorrect because it uses both the superlative "most" and the comparative suffix "-er" together, which is redundant.

  • Correct forms:
     • "more bitter" (comparative)
     • "most bitter" (superlative)

Other parts of the sentence are correct.

questions.q: This is on far a best ice cream I have ever had.
questions.s: (a) Explanation:- 'I have ever had' - jo aaj tak maine khai hai. Yani iss ice cream ka comparison aaj khai sab ice-cream se hai isliye superlative degree lagegi. or superlative degree ki intensity badhane ke liye 'by far' ka use hota hai. Isliye 'by far the best' ka use hoga.

questions.q: He runs (a) / more faster (b) / than I. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Faster' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'faster than.' Answer: (b). 'Faster' pehle se comparative hai, 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'faster than.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: India is already the third-largest / aviation market in/ terms of domestic travel. (SSC MTS Tier-01 08/05/23)
questions.s: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Third-largest' is a correctly used superlative adjective.

questions.q: She is (a) / more beautiful (b) / than her cousin. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'More beautiful' is correct for comparative degree. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'more beautiful' comparative degree ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).

questions.q: This is (a) / more better (b) / than that. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Better' is comparative; 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'better.' Answer: (b). 'Better' pehle se comparative hai, 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'better.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: This is (a) / very much exciting (b) / news. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Much' is redundant; correct form is 'very exciting.' Answer: (b). 'Much' extra hai, sahi form hai 'very exciting.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q:
It's important for media to be more responsibly and careful.

[MTS 09/8/2019 S3]
questions.s: The error in the sentence lies with the use of "more responsibly," where "responsibly" is incorrectly used as an adverb. Since the sentence requires an adjective to modify "media," the correct form should be "more responsible".

questions.q: What is the / price of this / fancy dress pink?
questions.s:
Adjectives typically come before the noun they modify.
The color of the dress, 'pink', is an adjective and it should come before the noun 'dress'.
Correct form : "What is the price of this fancy pink dress?”

questions.q: He is (a) / the more intelligent (b) / student in the school. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). Use 'most intelligent' for superlative. Answer: (b). Superlative ke liye 'more' nahi, 'most intelligent' chahiye. Jawab: (b).

questions.s: "Salary" is an uncountable noun, so "fewer" is incorrect. "Lower" is the correct adjective to compare salary.

questions.q: Of the two great cities (a)/ the former is (b)/ biggest. (c)/ No error (d)
o: Of the two great cities
questions.s: Use "the bigger" instead of "biggest.”

questions.q: This book is informative than entertaining.
questions.s:
The sentence contains an error. According to the rule, when comparing two qualities of a noun or pronoun, "more + positive degree" should be used instead of a comparative degree. In this case, "more informative" should be used instead of "informative."

The corrected sentence would be: "This book is more informative than entertaining."

o: method which we are suggesting
should be found out.
questions.s: Use comparative: "A simpler solution than this expensive method...".
